speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: Brother? Gilbert. From St Bride's, and the shop's shut, so I'm speaking for nothing.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Gilbert. I hear you.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: It's Richard's day. One and twenty. I have sent nothing. Have you?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Nothing. A letter written is not a letter on the road.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: A Stratford man was at the Bell. He says Father is being dunned again.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Who by?

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: Father owes the baker. No, not that baker. The other baker.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You have the sound of a list.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: The shoemaker. And the whittawer, for skins, which is a glover owing a glover.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Three shops.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: Three. Small sums, let run a year. I added them on a shop-ticket. I am not asking you to pay it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Read it.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: The other baker, one and forty shillings. The shoemaker, four and forty shillings and sixpence. The whittawer, fourteen and six.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Again.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: Forty-one. Forty-four and six. Fourteen and six. The ticket comes to five pound if you are strict with the pence. I call it near five pound. A shop-ticket is not a purse.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Fourteen and six is a sum I have already seen, in another ink.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: I don't know your ink. I know the whittawer's book. He has not asked me to ask you.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Which baker stands at the church porch on Sundays?

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: I don't know what you mean.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Never mind. I'm for home in a fortnight.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: A fortnight is a ride. It is not a purse.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then we are agreed. Five pound is the ticket. Near is your word. I will keep both, and pay neither tonight.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: Keep them. I have read it twice.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The shop is shut, you said. So this costs you nothing.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: Then take a full purse and an empty face. God keep you.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: And you.
